question.:question/problem: Given that $y=-\frac{1}{11}\cdot \ln{\left(x \right)}$, find the slope of the tangent at $x=1.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
To find the slope of the tangent at a given point, we have to find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ at that point.

Taking the derivative, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}&=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-\frac{1}{11}\cdot \ln{\left(x \right)}) \\ &=-\frac{1}{11}\cdot (\frac{1}{x}) \\ &=- \frac{1}{11 x}\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent at $x=1$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\big|_{x=1}&=\left(- \frac{1}{11 x}\right)\big|_{x=1} \\ &=- \frac{1}{11}\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Taking the derivative, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}&=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\log_{6}x+4\cdot \ln{\left(x \right)}) \\ &=(\frac{1}{x \ln{\left(6 \right)}})+4\cdot (\frac{1}{x}) \\ &=\frac{1}{x \ln{\left(6 \right)}}+\frac{4}{x}\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent at $x=1$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\big|_{x=1}&=\left(\frac{1}{x \ln{\left(6 \right)}}+\frac{4}{x}\right)\big|_{x=1} \\ &=\frac{1}{\ln{\left(6 \right)}} + 4\,.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Given the function $y=4\cdot x^{2}+\ln{\left(x \right)},$ the slope of the tangent line at $x=4$ is{{field-1}}.
question.:question/worked-solution:
To find the slope of the tangent at a given point, we have to find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ at that point.

Taking the derivative, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}&=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(4\cdot x^{2}+\ln{\left(x \right)}) \\ &=4\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(x^{2})+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\ln{\left(x \right)}) \\ &=4\cdot (2 x)+(\frac{1}{x}) \\ &=8 x+\frac{1}{x}\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent at $x=4$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\big|_{x=4}&=\left(8 x+\frac{1}{x}\right)\big|_{x=4} \\ &=8 (4)+\frac{1}{(4)} \\ &=\frac{129}{4}\,.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Given that $y=11\cdot x-8+8\cdot \log_{2}x$, find the slope of the tangent at $x=\frac{1}{\ln{\left(2 \right)}}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
To find the slope of the tangent at a given point, we have to find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ at that point.

Taking the derivative, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}&=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(11\cdot x-8+8\cdot \log_{2}x) \\ &=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(11\cdot x)-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(8)+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(8\cdot \log_{2}x) \\ &=11\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(x)-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(8)+8\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\log_{2}x) \\ &=11\cdot (1)-0+8\cdot (\frac{1}{x \ln{\left(2 \right)}}) \\ &=11+\frac{8}{x \ln{\left(2 \right)}}\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent at $x=\frac{1}{\ln{\left(2 \right)}}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\big|_{x=\frac{1}{\ln{\left(2 \right)}}}&=\left(11+\frac{8}{x \ln{\left(2 \right)}}\right)\big|_{x=\frac{1}{\ln{\left(2 \right)}}} \\ &=11+\frac{8}{(\frac{1}{\ln{\left(2 \right)}}) \ln{\left(2 \right)}} \\ &=11+8 \\ &=19\,.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Given that $y=10\cdot \ln{\left(x \right)}+10\cdot x^{2}-5\cdot x$, find the slope of the tangent at $x=1.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
To find the slope of the tangent at a given point, we have to find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ at that point.

Taking the derivative, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}&=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(10\cdot \ln{\left(x \right)}+10\cdot x^{2}-5\cdot x) \\ &=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(10\cdot \ln{\left(x \right)})+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(10\cdot x^{2})-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(5\cdot x) \\ &=10\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\ln{\left(x \right)})+10\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(x^{2})-5\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(x) \\ &=10\cdot (\frac{1}{x})+10\cdot (2 x)-5\cdot (1) \\ &=\frac{10}{x}+20 x-5\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent at $x=1$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\big|_{x=1}&=\left(\frac{10}{x}+20 x-5\right)\big|_{x=1} \\ &=\frac{10}{(1)}+20 (1)-5 \\ &=10+20-5 \\ &=25\,.\end{aligned}
$$
